segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I’m a-going to ask you these questions that they have written here. We are going to have a conversation in Cherokee. These students here might learn something from you talking and also, they are trying so the Cherokee language will not stop. The Cherokee language is declining.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I am having this sickness in my head, in the bone. They said it has those spots.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: The cancer?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I could tell because I was forgetting some things, but it is a little better.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Is it better now?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: It is not like it was. If I forget something, y’all will know the reason why.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, I guess it's better that you are understanding things better.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: They do hook you up to heal you and burn you (radiation). Something else will happen to you because my eyes are bothering me a little bit. That is what happens.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: And for some, they lose their teeth or lose their fingernails, but that didn’t happen to me. It was just my hair.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: God is helping you a little bit or even a lot.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I have been losing weight recently. When I was well last year, I weighed 200 lbs and now I weigh 140. They were just literally carrying me around. You could say it was dangerous, what happened to me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What is your name in English and in Cherokee what is your name?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: In English, my name is Andrew Hair. In Cherokee Isaac.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Isaac.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Is my name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where were you born, when you came to earth?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: The old hospital that was in Claremore.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Claremore.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Where I remember growing up was in Leach, was where we first lived. Then we moved. I was about five or six years old when we moved to the community where we are now. Near Amo, above where they call Kenwood, that was where my dad grew up. We came from there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What were the name of your parents?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: My father's name was Totem Hair and my mother was Annie. Used to be... My mother was from Leach.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I knew Woody Hair. Very good – Woody Hair was a prankster.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: That’s true. He is been like that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What was Woody’s name in Cherokee?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Tsusvwali was his name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: What was it?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Tsusvwali.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Tsusvwali. What was the meaning of that?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I think it is what they call a mill, a long time ago, when they hammered something, when they had those wheels hanging. That is what I think. I didn’t really understand. His self, he said his name was Tsusvwali, because all the young women were around him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He would talk about anything.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: That is true.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And some believed him.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: That is the way it was. When we were growing up, they would talk about everything. It was true until one day I grew up and matured, I found out. “They were really joking with me,” I thought. My first cousin, he is a little older than me. He was talking about going to school. They were playing ball somewhere. They were from somewhere that came and some of them were black people. They were out playing, us he was saying, he said, he was telling Tsusvwali. He said, “It’s easy to overcome them.” He said he told him, “We almost get into a fight.” He said, “I will tell you.” He said, “If he is thinking something about you, step on his foot real hard. They have soft feet,” he said. “A black person is easy to beat up, if you do that to him,” so he said. “We played ball again and they were defeating us,” he said. “They were pushing us around,” he said. “Then he pushed hard. I thought, ‘I am going to beat him up now!’ So I jumped hard and stepped on him and looked at him.” He said, “It made him mad even more, so pounded me.” And Tsusvwali said, “That never happened to me.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Woody was funny. I pastor at Steele. Woody used to go there and Brenda. There was some white people that came for a little while that were from Tennessee. They helped us fix the church building. One White among them from Tennessee liked to joke around. He said, “Hey Woody, do you have moonshine around here?” He said, “Yeah, when it’s not cloudy!” he said to him. Those other white people started falling around laughing. He was joking with one of those white people.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: He would say anything.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, then one time they were joking around out towards Belfonte. His name is Sevenstar. Woody would always take me when I had to go preach. He would say, "We are going." One time, they called me at Belfonte. Where they call Belfonte, there was a person there he got to know very quickly. He was the same way Woody is. They were joking. They started talking about deer. Boy, one time he said, “It was at night.” He said he took a big light. He said, “If you use it like that, those deer will stop. It blinds them,” he said. He had it like that, and they would just run by. It was not affecting them. He said he thought, “What’s happening?” Still again, he said, “There was a big deer that ran by, I still had it like this. It stopped just over there and when that deer turned around it was wearing sunglasses.”

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Last year – it’s been a long time ago – it has been 40 years since my dad was still living. My brother, my youngest brother, he was going to school. It was about this time, summertime. It was hot. He was fixing a car and that place in Kenwood was open where they shot pool. I was ready to go there. I didn’t finish fixing it and my brother's friend was going to come by and pick me up. I said, “If you don’t mind, I will borrow your car.” He had an old pickup. He said, “As long as you put gas, but you really have to pump those brakes.” I said, “OK.” I got ready and put some new pants on. Back then they used to call those shoes Jordan. I had those kind. There was a little store just over there, so went over there. I was ready. I was coming back. You know how it is, if rains just a little bit?

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yes.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: It had done that. I was coming, a deer came out right there, so I started stepping on the brakes. That deer tried to stop, but it slipped in the road. I hit it and it fell. I stopped. I thought it died, or something happened to it. I was looking. It wasn’t moving. I got out. It stood up and looked straight at me and shook its head. I thought, “Nothing happened.” It turned and jumped toward the fence and got hung up. I was watching it kick. I thought I better help it, but I took about two steps and it got off. It charged toward me! I was backing up – I ran into the truck. I had never been hit that hard. That deer was hitting me with his head. I was trying to run away from it. It was hitting me with its feet. It tore my pants and shoes. I couldn’t get away from it. Something happened and I caught it. When he would get loose, he would hit me in the eye hard, and I beat it up we were fighting going around. I was trying to kick it, but I couldn’t. It was scratching my knees. There was a hose in the back – they would get gas out with those. I went and got that and choked it. It was still getting loose, stepping on me. Its nose was bloody and so was mine. There was nobody going by, so it barely stopped when I let it go. It fell. I thought, just let it lay there. I thought it would be bad if I did that, so I put it in the back, and it was getting loose. I thought, “That’s not good,” when I got to the house. I was getting out. Atlosido was standing there and said, “What is happening to you?” I said, “I am fighting with a deer.” He said, “No!” I said, “Yes! It’s in the back.” When he looked back there, he said it was true. “It almost beat you up!” I went to Kenwood in my old pants.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It tore your new pants? You were wearing shoes called Jordan.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: They were expensive, too, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: [unintelligible], that deer was sticking its tongue out.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Some are dangerous, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I was telling them, “I kill deer and I don’t even use a gun. I am not lying either.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: If you told somebody, they would not believe you.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: We first fixed that deer before we left. Our friend and his brother lived close by – they came. They said, “Where did you kill it?” And I told them. They said, “Did you run over it?” I said, “No, I choked it.”

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: One time, I don’t know if you knew Buck Tanner that lived long time ago?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Yes, I knew Gvlvgini.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That is, Gvlvgini, one of his sons was bragging one time. That one boy said, “Yeah, my dad Buck, he killed a deer with a rock. Ahhh yeah.” They were bragging. He said, “how did he do it?” He said, “Well that deer tried to jump over a fence. He got hung on a fence, that deer,” he said. “Buck, my dad went over there and hit him on top of the head with that rock,” he said. It was true. They did not believe him the first time. And another one, it was at that time that Buck Tanner was friends with that game ranger. He came to Buck’s house about the time they were cooking that deer. The game ranger found out and said, “What you got cooking, Buck?” He said, “Aaah, we just got a cow cooking,” he was telling him. That game ranger was wanting to take that deer meat, so he told him, said “Well Buck, don’t be killing no more cows.” Where did you say you grew up a minute ago?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I was first born in Leach and then, where we live where they say Gvnid school, just there. I grew up there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I guess it’s different now where you grew up.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: That is true. When I first went to school I went and I just went for a little while. It seemed like it was about then. I was just about five or six years old when we left and that’s when I started at where Gvnid is. It went to the sixth grade, then I went to school at Kenwood. When I finished the eighth grade, then I went towards the water. Then I finished there. That was where I ended going to school. I never went to school anywhere else.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Sometimes does your mind go back to where you grew up and think, “This is how it was?”

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Yes, I can picture a lot. Like here in Tahlequah, we would come here. We have some relatives here, but forget. I was little, but I do remember. Where the creek is in town, it was near there. It was not like it is now.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It is not like that anymore.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Where the old hospital was, when you come in.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I was afraid when we had to go there. When someone was sick, they would end it there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s true.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Back then, we brought a lunch. We would have a blanket laying outside about this time. We would wait. I remember the waiting room was small at the hospital. I was afraid for something to happen to me there. I was thinking they will kill you. And nowadays I think that even more. When it was almost dark, I would think there must really be some tsigilis in there. They say that is how it was. I am not making a mistake.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You thought they were killing them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: When you were healthy where did you work?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Everywhere, but the first time I started, I went to Tulsa. Two of my brothers were working there and I got on with them. They hired me. They made steel, they melted it. I was doing that, pouring them in.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Gah-lee.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I got big for a little while. You really had to work then. Something happened – that thing they used to melt with broke and some got laid off. I looked for work, so I went to a place where they made steel. That is what I did in the past. I would make something. When it would shut down, I would get a job somewhere they were building. I could do that, too. And just last year I left for over 20 years. I went to Nvdagi. They gave me a job. They would go everywhere, fixing those things. They either made or tore down those big metal buildings and were builders. It was really good to work there. They came to Pryor, where those big places are. I worked there. I told them, “This is where I left from.” When we got finished, they sent me, too. I was able to take two weeks off, I was told. For that long, I was able to take time off. But they said, “Before you go there, go to Maryland, somewhere called Columbia, Maryland.” So I went, but they made a mistake, because when I got there they were almost done. They said, “We didn’t call you!” They talked to me and I told them. They said, “Just take your leave. Just take your vacation.” I said, “OK.” I was looking around. I found some lady from overseas that had lived here a long time, so went that way. So I stayed there for about six years. It was a good place to be. But then, when Dad and Mom started to get old, I told her, “I better go home.” So I went home. I really saw some interesting things there. I really did like to fish. We would go there. It was near big water. I don’t know what the name of that place is there, in Cherokee. Natives have named that place there. They called it Tvskohana River. It flowed, there was a big dam. I would fish below there, and I would catch different kinds of fish. I haven’t seen any like that. I don’t know the names of them. But when the big water rose, the water would rise, too, and when it dropped it was a good time to catch something. I would catch a lot of eel. When I first caught one, I thought it was a snake. It was this long. I was going to kill it. I don’t know what kind they were. There was some natives there. They asked for it and I gave it to them. Then later I caught another one. It was a little bigger and I gave them, too. The woman said, “You don’t eat them?” I said, “I don’t eat snakes.” She said, “That’s not snakes. Those are eels!” She said, “If you catch one this big, take it. I will fix it.” So, I did that. When I looked good, an eel is just like a fish. It has like, ears it breathes with. She fixed it so that it was good to eat. There was some that were like bass that were coming from the big water. When you caught one like that, you didn’t know what to do. They were big, but I would catch them. They were 4 ft long. That was too much for two people to eat that. They were also good to eat.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How many siblings did you have?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Eight.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Eight, yeah.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Four girls and four of us boys.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You boys... What about your grandmother and grandfather, what were their names?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Dinusdi was the old man. His name was Nick Hair and grandmother the old lady's name was Walisi Molly.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Molly, that’s it. That is where Woody’s son got his name, because his name is Nick, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: There is another one that used to live—or, actually, lives in the area. His name is Nick, too. But I think they say that one is just adopted.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, yeah.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: You probably knew Lewi Houston.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Houston, yeah, I think so.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Him and his wife – Nikkie was the name. There was another one that was living. Her name was Mary, that lives somewhere near Oklahoma City. They said they were adopted. They already had them and then – Som was his name – their biological child came later. He also passed away the other day.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I was working at Wickliffe school at the time of your dad's funeral, I remember now. And then Woody’s funeral near Kenwood ball field.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: That is when I was sick. It is much better nowadays. The people were talking about it in the past, but I was not able to come.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, that’s true.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Not until recently I started walking, but was telling them, “I can’t go very far walking. I have to take care of myself.” I am getting stronger. It’s getting better.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It was in Woody’s name they built that building in Kenwood and it really is a beautiful building.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: There is a big building? I have not been there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: You haven’t? Yeah, there is a beautiful building. When they opened it up, there was lots of people that came there. Your parents and your grandmother and your grandfather. Did they know of some medicine from the woods, for instance root medicine?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: They really did know but back then. Most of the people knew things like that. I was talking to that one when they first were finding out about cancer. The elders really believed there was a medicine for that. You would not hardly hear about that. My dad really did know how to do things. Someone came to visit about the time I came back. They said they were finding cancer. They said it only be about a month. I knew him, too. He gave him something to drink. He passed away just the other day – his heart killed him. The cancer was gone. It is true. They did know something. They were telling me they were finding something. I was thinking it would have been good if they told me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Ah man yeah.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I knew where what they knew came from. It was from the experts.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It’s true.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: You can’t put a price on it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It’s true.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: It is not good if someone is trying to sell it, they would say.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: I was taught one time, for instance, you are not really supposed to put a price on it, but for instance. I guess that is how it was a long time ago. For instance, they were trading medicine for food. Even if you were given a dollar, the medicine is going to work as long as you show appreciation. They said even if you have a quarter or a dollar, some really did price it at a lot.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Some elder man was telling me long time ago, like, that if someone asks for something and if you help them, he said, they are supposed to be as happy as you are for helping them. There is no limit, because one day you are going to need something, he would say. That is what I was asking him. I said, “Why do some work bad things?” He said, “People are like that. Just like they are all different. Some are friendly and kind and some are bad that do bad and look for bad,” he said. “That is why when man was first came, that is why they think different. How they think is how you will know them,” he said. “By knowing them that is how you decide how you are going to be yourself,” he told me. He said, “If someone does you bad, is that what you want to do? Or if someone does you good, would you rather that? You have to choose,” he said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Your parents, did they meet just somewhere there, in Kenwood?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Yes, my grandmother, just to the east of here where they say Lost City, she grew up there somewhere. I could be mistaken, but I think she said there was 13 of them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Siblings?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Let’s see how many did she say? They were written somewhere. I think there were three girls and the rest were boys. And the old lady's mother, her relatives lived towards Jay. She was a Skruggins, there and also related to the Summerfields. And I think she was from there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah, there are some that live there by the name Summerfield and in Euchie there are some Summerfield.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: My grandmother, I could be mistaken, those White Killers that lived, they were related too, I think she said. I didn’t understand it good. I think now it would have been better if I would have listened when they would tell me things like that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: There really was some with the name White Killer where I come from in Jay. There was a little place they made what they call computer boards. I worked there for a little while, for about two years. We made boards for those planes that fly around. They put on there to make them go. And for cars, like the Ford Company, we made them. To put on trains, we made them. Then one day I talked to the boss, and I said, “What about these boards we are making?” I said, “You sell them to the airplane company?” He said, “Yes, it helps it to fly.” He said, “These you are making help it to fly.” I thought, “Gaw, if I make a mistake and they take and sell it, and the plane goes down somewhere. If that board is not correct, whose fault is it going to be if it falls off?”

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: It will go back there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: “They are going to trace it back to where it was made, and it will come back to you,” he said.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: It will point to you.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That was when I quit.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: When I went toward Maryland, some people hired me. It was back then, there was something going on overseas. And they blew up New York, just after that. He said, “We need some help.” I said, "What do you need?” He said, “I am putting in some rooms for something not to get in – Sterile environment they call.” He said, “Do you know how?” I said, “I don’t.” He said, “It is just like building a room.” I said, “OK.” So they hired me. Over there, where [Unclear] They wore those whites, we had to do that. Then we got called over there to go underground. It was... I don’t remember how far it was. We would go down or get in. There were soldiers there watching. They had guns. Some were there from overseas – Anigvli Angvtsino and some Antsawodige were there. Sometime later, Anitsu Dalone. They had that picture on how to do it. That is what we were doing. We made one just about this size. It had a straight round hole – it was 20 feet. There was a metal thing, this big. We made the doors the same, heavy and thick. There was lead on there. It was because what they call radiation could not get through. They were saying, “That may have contaminated you the other day.” I couldn’t say it was interesting when we were working there. That I am, was, amazed by what they were doing. When they were blowing up airplanes. There were some from there that were working there. I didn’t understand. I was thinking, “Why are they doing that?” It wasn’t for me to say. One was a German. When he found out I was native, he was talking to me all the time. He would say, “When you get done eating, let’s go somewhere.” He would ask me questions. He said, “What is your home like?” I said just like it was. He said, “do y’all still hunt for buffalo?” I told him no. He said, “Y’all don’t wear clothes like they have?” I said, “Those are different natives.” Back then I had long hair. He said, “I will pay if I can go somewhere and get yours done like that. I want a picture of you.” I said, “Why?” I showed him a picture of my dad, like that. He said, “Can I borrow it?” I said, “I will just give it to you.” And so, he took it and went back overseas. About three months went by. A paper came, about yay long. When I opened it, his name was on there. It came from Germany. I unwrapped it – it was my dad's picture. He made one bigger, with a pencil. It is beautiful. I have a big picture of him now. He was telling me, “If you ever go overseas, come here.” He was wanting to come to the area to see me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Do you remember sometimes when you were growing up? For instance, Woody really helped people a long time ago. Like if someone was sick, they would go and help them. They called it gawdugi. Or if someone passed away, they would have a wake service at their house and then the next morning they would take them to the cemetery. You remember that don’t you?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I really do. They don’t do that nowadays. That is what happened to my grandmother, her, and my great grandmother. That is where it ended. I don’t remember them doing that with others recently, the youngest, but I do know that is where we went. I was small back then. I think it was in Bull Hollow somewhere, when I think about it. They would hire us children. We were yey tall. We would go get water, because nobody had water back then. We would go there and get water. We would draw it out of a creek, and there was a separate spot for drinking. There was a spring just over there, on a ridge. We would get that from there. There was one boy – I can’t even say who it was – there was several of us. I would get aggravated with him. When they would send him to get water, he would just get it from the creek. But it was good to drink back then.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yes, back then.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Just the other day I went out that way. I was thinking, trying to remember where that creek was. There was a road that went up the hill, but I couldn’t find it. I don’t know if it’s there nowadays. We went there for several days. Back then it was good. We would lay outside. I can’t hardly say who it was. There wasn’t hardly any white people in this area. They have only recently started being aggravating.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: They are aggravating.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: It woke up when you said that.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Do you remember that road that was by Steele Cemetery? Long time ago there was a spring.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Yes, we would go to Steele, too. Dvgvdosgi was the pastor. We would go there, too. When you went past there, just on this side there was a good creek. There was a good place to swim. We would go there – nobody hardly went there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It is really different now, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: That’s true.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It’s wooded now. They say there was a road there at one time, by the spring. Then they built a bridge.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: When they built a bridge, it ruined it. What about if you come by there, they call it Tyo Church. I don’t remember. I think I have been there once. I think they were fixing something there. I was just really a boy when me and my dad went there. I think he took some lumber over there. I don’t really know. He went and got them from somewhere. I don’t know if he gave them that, but we did go over there. They were on the roof in the back, fixing something. That was the only time that I have been to Tyo. It feels scary when you go by there, from what they talk about.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That is true. Did they say it was dangerous?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Across from there, if you go by where the curve is, if you turn there toward the water, we would go there. We would put a boat in the water, when we would go gigging, a long time ago. Sometimes, we would just go there for a little while, because of something making noise. You really could hear something. Just like if it was trying to ruin it for someone. It would be going under water or it would be making a sound. When it did that, we came back. But you always heard it. We really did get those fish. There really was something there, I believe over where Tyo is.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Me too. One time when I was just a boy, we went there just across from Tyo. We brought a boat. They told the two of us to stay and build a fire. They said, “We will just cook them right here.” OK, so me and my friend built a fire. We were just sitting there. The others got in the boat and then later they came back quickly. We put the boat back in and they said, “Put it out.” We were thinking, “What is the reason they were saying ‘let’s go’?” Then we put it out. We left there, that is when they told us something was throwing rocks in the water. As we got closer, the rocks sounded like they were landing closer. They said, “Gaw! There is something there!” Then sometime later, I told Woody. He said, “Ah there is not anything there.” What do they call beaver in Cherokee? Beaver–they have the wide tail... I forget.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Doya.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yes, doya. “That is what lives there,” he said. A beaver, really will...

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: ...slap its tail.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Slap its tail.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: The other day.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: That is what was scaring y’all.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: My other cousin's son, his son was talking about he said he went to the water and there was a man that lived down the hill named David Jumper.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh, David Jumper?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: He said he got to the water. He said, “De-wi, I came to swim, if you don’t mind.” He said, “No but you better watch out. Something is around. It is pretty mad.” So he asked him what it was and it was daytime. Darrel said, “They say it is a beaver, but I don’t know." He said he thought I wouldn’t be scared of that, so he went down the hill. He said when he got there, he did hear something making noise in the water on the rocks, then in the water. He thought, “What is it?” So he went around there and it was out of the water or getting out of the water. It had something in its mouth chewing on it and its cheeks were like this. He said it looked at him, and started doing this. “It was this tall,” he said, “It was bigger than a midget,” he said. He left from over there. He said he was doing his tail like that. It looked dangerous. “I wasn’t going to mess with that beaver,” he said.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It was like this.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: It was ready for a fight.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: And my wife’s brother – you knew him – his name was Donald King, the late Mauden’s son.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Yeah, I have heard of him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: He said they were looking for wild onion near Tyo, close to there, just on the other side. They were really working. He said, “Then later, I looked over there. It was a black panther sitting over there. Its tail was doing this and looking at us,” he said. He said he told his wife to move slowly. “Let’s leave real slow. Don’t move fast because if you move fast it is going to charge at us.” So, he said that black panther was looking at us. Its tail was going like this, then later it got down and went the other way, he said. Really, there is one there, because one time I left Steele Church when it was dark. Like you said, it is kind of scary at Tyo. I went around where that curve is, something black was sitting there. It moved away quickly. I was thinking it was a cougar when I looked at it.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Cougars do exist, I seen them twice. I have heard of them several times in the past when I was a hunter. One time, it has probably been 40 years ago – what was the name of that church on 33? There was a white barn, just over there. There is a crossroad there. You go down the hill, then turn to the north. Curtis Snell used to live there.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Oh yeah.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I went that way to go visit one time. It was in the summer, when it is hot. I turned and I had the windows open and the dust was flying. When I got there, I went that way those Snells lived, way over there. It wasn’t even a mile, maybe half. There was a fence and something flew by. I put my brakes on and kicked the dust up and it landed over there. It was about this tall. It sat there and looked at me and its tail was doing that. It happened quickly. It got loose and went over the other fence. It ran that way. There were trees. It was running away doing this and its tail was doing this. I saw it good – it was a cougar. I got there and I told them, “I seen a cougar.” They said to me, “You are drunk! You are lying!” I said, “Say that when they eat the cows.”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I do know there was a black one like that at the house. It never messed with the cows. I was surprised. We had calves – we were afraid for those, but it did not do nothing. Maybe it was just passing through.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: That is what they say, they just pass through. They say it will come back in several years, or its offspring will come back by. I saw another cougar where Locust Grove is when you come up that hill from the lake. Where they call it pump back, where that curve is. It did the same thing. It ran off that hill and ran by. It was in the evening. I got a good look at it. They do exist.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, they do exist there, ain’t it. No telling.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Do they scream out? Like a woman, ain’t it? One time, I heard that I was calling cows early in the morning. It was about four in the morning. It screamed. I thought it was a woman.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, just like woman.

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: I thought it was a woman screaming. It scared me, that was it.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: One time we had dismissed at Steele, we were standing outside, Woody Hair and George. George was not afraid of anything. It screamed just like a woman near the creek behind Steele. He said, “Somebody is out there. It sounds like a woman.” George said, “I will go see.” But strangely, he didn’t see anything. Woody was saying it was a cougar. He said, “Hey George, it’s a panther.” But he kept walking. He didn’t see anything. It really did scream like a woman.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: If it is walking, they said you can’t hear its footsteps.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Did you know the late Unvdatlvgi Bud’s boys? They were drinkers. One time we were staying near Tyo. They were drinking. They got there late at night. They were saying, “This is where there are tsigilis living here in Tyo.” One of them that was half drunk said, “I wouldn’t be scared of anything. They are just tsigilis.” Then they talked about how if you go around the church, you could see something. He said, “I’ll go around it several times. I’m not scared of anything. I will run it off.” They told him to get out, so he went around. Then after a while he came back to the car we were sitting in. Who was it that was talking about it? It might have been one of those Sap boys. He said he didn’t find anything. He said, “I will go around again.” So went around and in the back on the north side was a big hole under the house. He was over there saying, “Look! Look! a tsigili grabbed me!” He was like this. He said something did grab him, then he started hollering, “Help me! Help me!” Then after a while he was almost crying. One time a long time ago, someone lost a monkey that was in the church. He was crying and they really did barely pull him back. Then we got back in, he was still crying when we left from there. He was saying, “Grab me, tsigili! Grab me!”

segments.speaker: dianna-guffey
segments.translation: Something really did grab him.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yeah, someone lost a monkey back then. It got loose, that was it.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I don’t know if it was a ghost or what it was. A long time ago it was in the fall. We were still in school. We were playing football. We were practicing. We went home. I don’t know if you know Wil Tsatsi? They would say Willy Raper. I was with his two sons. We ate a little bit, and they said, “We will take you home.” We came up the hill. The moon was really bright – it was after dark. Nowadays, someone lives there now on the hill but back then there was one house. There was some white person that would come there just sometimes. He lived in town. He was a hunter. We were driving along, talking. When we got to the curve he said, “Look!” James was his name. He was sitting in the back and we looked toward the trees. It was a flame doing this. Mark was driving and he went faster and that thing went faster, too, just like if it was chasing us. It went close by. It was clear that it hit us on the side. The car went like that. Then it got bright. Boy, our heads were doing this. We got to the house. When we looked, there was not a mark anywhere. We saw it good. It was this big. It was raised up about this high. When they went home, they said, “We are going around toward town.” He was telling his brother to get in the back. He was saying, “No, I’m going to get in the front.” It really was strange. But what did they call those a long time ago? Jack with a light? It was one like that. My dad would tell me. I have seen one like that before. It came out where the house is. There was a bridge across from there, in the fall you would see it. Just like if someone was carrying a light, playing around. It would be swinging, jumping around. Like, it would fade away then later, it would come out again. That was what my dad was talking about the time I was going to school then, when I first seen one. I said, “Look what’s happening over there.” He said, “Huh, it came back. It would come here all the time last year,” he said. There was a house that they grew up in around the curve, back then where my grandmother used to live. He said in the summer they would sit outside after they ate. He said there was a big field and the trees were way over there. You could see them coming and they would go by and that is what they would be doing was playing around. There would be several of them and if you were up early, you would see them coming back, going back where they came from he said. So I guess they existed.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Could they have been little people?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I really can’t say, but it could have been. But I have people that were hunting, talking about seeing it somewhere. When they were lost, they would follow that then they would come out somewhere, they would say. One time, we lost a dog while we were hunting. It went into the refuge. It was not coming back. I went to look for it. It was almost dark over there on that ridge. Someone had a fire built, so I went that way. I was going that way. I wasn’t thinking anything. Then I was going down the hill. We were kind of like walking in a hollow, then the fire was over there, so I went that way just the same. So now it was really dark, so we just went home. I was telling my grandmother. She said, “You are not supposed to go there! If you do go there, take something like sugedi or something.” I said, “Why?” She said, “There is some Mexicans buried there.” I said, “Where did they come from?” I thought she was talking about real Mexicans. Instead, it was what the elders used to call gypsies. She said they are buried there. She knew that person that used to raise horses a long time ago. She said they would go there when they had their burials. She said they are buried there. If there is a flame, we are not supposed to bother them.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That really is interesting.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: She said when one passed away they would put anything with value that they had in there with them. Some were wealthy and it is not good if you do that. They will take you with them, she said. The last time I was back over there, it was about dark. I could see a fire this tall [gesture] someone built. That was the sign that was given.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: That there was gypsies buried there.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: She said it was different if there was money buried there. It would be blue.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It is true that if there is money hidden somewhere, they have something hired to watch over it. The yellow money, like you said, they would hide it in the ground, and they would doctor it. That happened one time...where was it? On the other side of Long Springs. I forget who it was that was talking about it. He was Cherokee – you probably know him. He said it burns every year, the money, the flame is blue. They would say that there is money hidden there. He said one time that happened he knew just where the flame was, so the next morning, he said he went there and was digging. Boy, he said he heard something, like there were lots of horses running toward him. He said the ground was shaking and he said it scared him. He said he ran from there. He didn’t even see a horse. They must have put that there to watch over the money.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I don’t know if I can talk about what you are talking about. It is strange. I have never done anything. I have just been told things like that. They have made room, and if you don’t obey, they say something will happen to you. I think about it and that is what happened to me, I think. A long time ago, I came back from the army. I went to Mom’s. I was asleep. I slept for a little while. I was dreaming something strange. It was kind of like what you are talking about. I know when it was. I was standing, there was several of us. We could see some going, pulling a horse wagon. They were digging, putting something in there. In my dream, when they left I went to go look and I found something, but I didn’t see it. The horses you said? I was digging. I could hear the horses running around, going around, their footsteps, then people started talking. First they were mad. I was scared, but I kept digging. Their voices sounded like men, but you could not see them. They were saying, “Stop! Break from what you are doing! We are going to do something to you!” I was afraid, but I kept digging. Then they were saying, “If you stop, we will give you this or we will do this for you.” They kept talking more and I was afraid and those horses were as they were. As I began to dig deeper, they were even more afraid. They were saying, “Look what are we going to do!” Just like kids. Then the shovel I had hit something. It made a loud sound. It was just like something happened to them. Some were in pain and they hollered and said, “He found it!” My dream ended there. I asked Mom what it was. She had gravy and bread on the table before I went to sleep. I said, “What kind of gravy was that?” I thought about the dream I had for a long time. I asked the readers to take a look. They all told me the same thing. I know where it is at. I never bothered anything or tried anything. I look over there, when I go by. I know good where it was.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Where it is.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: But it has been a long time. That is why things happen to me now, because I didn’t listen. For some it makes room.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yes, that’s true.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: You can’t say it might be fooling me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: How much more we got? I am going to ask you this last. It’s asking, in about 20 years, if we are still living on this earth, do you think that the Cherokee language is going to fade away or what?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: As for me, what we say... how we talk... if you think about your past it was different a long time ago. That is how much it has changed. Just like we are saying, it is going to change even more. How they are teaching these, they truly are trying, but it is not.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: It is not really the right way. The sound is different, ain’t it?

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: That is what I was telling them the other day when they were talking about it. When they speak, they have learned it from studying a paper and where they grew up. I was telling them, but how we say it when we talk it will not be like that in 20 years. It will be no more. If we get lucky and live that long there will not hardly be anyone living to talk to. We are going to have to learn how. They are teaching them or they are going to learn how we are talking, but that will not happen.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: A lot has changed from the speakers that lived long time ago. You know as well as I do, when the elders were living.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Just like the beaver we are talking about. I know it when I hear it. I think about some of what is happening to me, just like if I see someone I know I forget their name.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yes, me too.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Or I may know their name and say, “Who is this?” Or if I am talking about something, I will run out. My head bothers me.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: We are all just like that.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: Another thing, it is not just the Cherokee that are losing it. The other natives that live in the area say the same thing. I came here some time ago. I was feeling pretty good. I came with my niece. There were some kind of natives here from the north. I think they were called Anomi and they were looking at a way to save their language so they will not lose it. I was sitting there thinking about it. I was thinking to myself, “We don’t know what to do.” This now, no matter how much knowledge they have from school, when you are talking to them, they will run out of understanding, just the same if they were talking to you. You can tell because you will not understand it all. It is the same for you. If you could fix that, but how could you do it? We are not students, for reason being, if they would teach them while they are growing up, but these students are just learning what they have been taught, not like it was. A long time ago, someone was asking me where I went to school. I said I didn’t go to school, I was just repeating people. So, I guess I just learned how they're talking. That is how it began, I was thinking. They also talk about where they went to school somewhere and got a whipping and was scolded. Maybe that did happen, but if a person makes an effort, it will not perish or lose it, I believe. I have got whipping for speaking Cherokee, but it did not make me stop.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Yes, that is true.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I didn’t make it a habit.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: No matter how much they were hitting you in the head.

segments.speaker: andrew-hair
segments.translation: I was glad I learned to speak English and to understand and count and the things that I learned. There is no difference in what I know. It might be just being hardheaded. I was able to learn both. Last year, I was hanging around with the Creeks. You could understand what I was saying but I have forgotten now, just like the Mexicans. I used to talk with them. If it is written I can understand more, but the reason for that is because the white people taught me to write in school. I was curious because I liked to learn things.

segments.speaker: guy-soldier
segments.translation: Well, I am glad. I am glad we had this conversation.
